title: The Forgotten Crown
subtitle: A Sovereign's Songbook & Thematic Analysis
genre: Traditional & Contemporary Scottish Folk / Bothy Ballads / Celtic Folk-Rock
hook: Traditional Scottish folk and gritty political folk-rock tracing the suppressed 1689 Claim of Right, Freeport corporate feudalism, and the reclamation of unalienable popular sovereignty.
thesis: The Forgotten Crown outlines a comprehensive, expert-level blueprint for a full-length concept album by The Shady River Bard. The album explores historical subjugation, the orchestrated division of the working class, and the eventual awakening of a populace to their inherent, unalienable sovereignty under the 1689 Claim of Right and the ancient principle of Salvo Jure Cujuslibet (saving the right of anyone). By interweaving constitutional history with contemporary economic struggles, the album demonstrates that history is a living weapon wielded by the oppressed, and that healing societal divisions is the prerequisite to enforcing popular sovereignty.

musical_direction.genre_and_style: Traditional and Contemporary Scottish Folk, Bothy Ballads, Celtic Folk-Rock. 4/4 Strathspey rhythms, driving marches, and sparse acoustic deconstructions.
instrumentation: Scottish Traditional Cello (sul tasto, rhythmic bass)
musical_direction.vocal_delivery: Raw, weathered, working-class baritone (Dick Gaughan style). Authentic enunciation, emotional gravity, and fierce moral conviction.
musical_direction.narrative_arc: Trajectory from melancholic observation to urgent frustration, to archival intellectual discovery, ending in triumphant collective resolve.

acts.title: Act I: The Imposed Division
acts.description: Observing the decay of the community through poverty, hollow party politics, and the corporate acquisition of public lands. Establishing that societal divisions are artificially orchestrated to distract the populace from their common plight.

acts.title: Act II: Descent into the Archives
acts.description: Unearthing the suppressed truths of the 1707 Treaty of Union, the transformation of public lands into deregulated Freeport SEZs, and the institutional silencing of ancient rights.

acts.title: Act III: Constitutional Awakening
acts.description: Discovering the irrefutable Scottish constitutional mechanism 'saving the right of anyone,' issuing direct instructions to the government through the Stirling Directive, and healing manufactured class divisions.

acts.title: Act IV: International Appeal & Popular Sovereignty
acts.description: Recalling the Convention of Estates via the Edinburgh Proclamation and appealing to the UN Special Committee on Decolonization (C-24), culminating in the resolute declaration that sovereignty rests forever with the people.

constitutional_matrix.pillar: The Claim of Right (1689) vs 1707 Annexation
constitutional_matrix.core_causes: The 1689 Claim of Right established that sovereignty rests inherently with the people of Scotland, who retain the right to depose monarchs who breach community trust. The 1707 Treaty operated as an involuntary annexation, superimposing Westminster parliamentary absolutism.
constitutional_matrix.manifestation: Westminster exercises unchecked legislative authority, while domestic working-class communities are powerless to prevent resource extraction and deindustrialization.
constitutional_matrix.societal_outcome: Subjugation under a colonial administrative model, broken by the rediscovery that parliamentary absolutism is unlawful under Scottish constitutional law.

constitutional_matrix.pillar: Corporate Feudalism & Plunder of the Common Good
constitutional_matrix.core_causes: The ancient Scottish legal doctrine of 'The Common Good' protects collective land and municipal assets in perpetuity for public benefit. Neoliberal privatization bypasses this safeguard via Freeports and Special Economic Zones (SEZs).
constitutional_matrix.manifestation: Deregulated corporate fiefdoms, suspended environmental and labor standards, and offshore asset stripping that alienates citizens from the wealth of their own land.
constitutional_matrix.societal_outcome: Entrenched poverty and manufactured wage competition, deliberately engineered to keep workers too exhausted to mount a unified constitutional defense.

constitutional_matrix.pillar: Salvo Jure Cujuslibet ('Saving the Right of Anyone')
constitutional_matrix.core_causes: An ancient Scottish parliamentary procedure passed at the close of every legislative session, explicitly preserving private rights against prejudiced, unnotified, or corrupt statutory overreach.
constitutional_matrix.manifestation: Proves that Scottish constitutional tradition prioritizes the citizen's inherent rights over legislative authority, establishing that no Act of Union could lawfully extinguish popular sovereignty.
constitutional_matrix.societal_outcome: An unassailable legal foundation empowering contemporary citizens to dismantle Westminster's claims of supreme authority.

constitutional_matrix.core_causes: The failure of parliamentary party politics necessitates direct civic action. Sovereign citizens possess the legal right to instruct their elected representatives, not merely elect them as masters.
constitutional_matrix.manifestation: Civic mandates declaring Westminster legislation null and void within Scotland, followed by the Edinburgh Proclamation demanding the recall of the Scottish Convention of Estates.
constitutional_matrix.societal_outcome: Inversion of the power structure, proving working people can organize independently of party machines to reclaim governance.

constitutional_matrix.core_causes: With domestic British courts exhausted and structured to protect parliamentary absolutism, the crisis moves to the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization (C-24) under UN Resolution 1514 (XV).
constitutional_matrix.manifestation: Petitions documenting political subjugation, economic extraction, and territorial military occupation presented before international human rights bodies.
constitutional_matrix.societal_outcome: Transforms the independence question from an internal domestic dispute into an international human rights imperative, forcing global scrutiny upon the UK state.

exhibits.title: Exhibit I: The Dust of Estates
exhibits.subtitle: The Memory of the Soil & Suppressed Rights (Track 1 & 2)
exhibits.caption: Ancient standing stones and ruined croft walls rise through the morning mist of the Scottish Highlands.
exhibits.analysis: The land itself holds the memory of common ownership and unextinguished rights. Beneath centuries of political maneuvering and industrial displacement, the soil bears witness to the sovereignty of the populace.
exhibits.quote: The earth does not forget. Beneath the concrete, the soil holds the memory of the common good.

exhibits.title: Exhibit II: Corporate Feudalism & The Freeport
exhibits.subtitle: Special Economic Zones & Commons Plunder (Track 3 & 6)
exhibits.caption: Cold industrial cranes, barbed wire perimeters, and tax-exempt shipping containers carve through ancient coastal common lands.
exhibits.analysis: Under the guise of modern economic renewal, Freeports strip public oversight and worker protections. The Common Good—land held in trust for all citizens—is auctioned to transnational conglomerates, turning citizens into tenants.
exhibits.quote: They slice the bread so thin and make us beg for crumbs, while corporate fiefdoms claim our native shores.

exhibits.title: Exhibit III: The Archivist's Midnight
exhibits.subtitle: Unearthing Salvo Jure Cujuslibet (Track 7 & 8)
exhibits.caption: A single tallow candle illuminates vellum manuscripts, wax seals, and dusty legislative records in an Edinburgh vault.
exhibits.analysis: In the quiet of midnight, deep within the legal archives, the protagonist discovers the golden clause: Salvo Jure Cujuslibet. No statute of annexation or act of bribery can lawfully strip a sovereign citizen of their inherent constitutional birthright.
exhibits.quote: Saving the right of anyone. The right of everyone. The sovereignty of the people cannot be extinguished.

exhibits.title: Exhibit IV: The Stirling Directive
exhibits.subtitle: Inverting the Pyramid of Power (Track 11 & 12)
exhibits.caption: Citizens gather upon the ramparts of Stirling Castle, holding signed civic mandates declaring popular sovereignty over parliament.
exhibits.analysis: The Stirling Directive rejects the passive posture of petitioning an unsympathetic parliament. By issuing direct instructions to representatives under the Claim of Right, the populace exercises the authority that ministers only hold in trust.
exhibits.quote: We do not beg for what is ours. We direct the crown; we instruct the state.

exhibits.title: Exhibit V: The Sovereign People
exhibits.subtitle: UN Committee of 24 & United Awakening (Track 14 & 15)
exhibits.caption: A multitude of Scottish working-class voices assemble peacefully in the Great Hall, their faces illuminated by dawn breaking over Edinburgh.
exhibits.analysis: The ultimate triumph of the album: orchestrated divisions crumble when working people recognize their shared plight. Standing before the international community and United Nations C-24, the sovereign people claim their place.
exhibits.quote: No parliament is sovereign here. The people are the crown.

tracks.title: Prologue: The Dust of Estates
tracks.summary: The earth does not forget the rights of its people. We are walking on the dust of estates, but the memory remains.
tracks.narrative_role: The earth does not forget the rights of its people. We are walking on the dust of estates, but the memory remains.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The earth does not forget.
Beneath the concrete, beneath the iron and the endless noise,
The soil holds the memory of the common good.
They told us the union was a voluntary pact, a shared crown.
But the stones of this land remember the theft.
They remember the annexation of our voice.

[Verse 2]
We walk upon the dust of estates.
A sovereign people, reduced to tenants in our own home.
The parliaments speak in distant halls, claiming an absolute right,
While the ancient laws sleep in the shadows of the archives.
They engineered this division, kept us fighting for scraps,
So we would not look down, and see the strength beneath our feet.

[Outro]
Listen to the wind. It whispers a forgotten truth.
The right of anyone. The right of everyone.
The sovereignty of the people cannot be extinguished by the pen of a king.
It is time to remember.
pull_quotes: The earth does not forget.
The parliaments speak in distant halls, claiming an absolute right,

tracks.title: The Orchestrated Divide
tracks.summary: Social issues, poverty, and the artificial division of the working class.
tracks.narrative_role: Social issues, poverty, and the artificial division of the working class.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They built the fences high, but they built the anger higher,
Set neighbour against neighbour round a fabricated fire.
The factories are empty, the ships are sold for scrap,
While we fight over the pennies that fall right off their lap.
You do not know the puppeteer when you are staring at the strings,
You only see the fist that the other puppet brings.

[Chorus]
It’s an orchestrated divide!
Keep the weary working class looking side to side!
If we never look up, we will never see the crown,
Just another generation, beaten out and broken down.
Yes, they keep us broken down.

[Verse 2]
I watched old Jimmy lose the farm his father cleared by hand,
Now it is leased to a corporation from a foreign land.
And the boys down at the pub, they blame the men across the street,
While the politicians laugh from a very comfortable seat.
They slice the bread so thin, and they make us beg for crumbs,
Drowning out the truth with the beating of their drums.

[Chorus]
It’s an orchestrated divide!
Keep the weary working class looking side to side!
If we never look up, we will never see the crown,
Just another generation, beaten out and broken down.
Yes, they keep us broken down.

[Bridge]
They need us blind! They need us weak!
They need us too afraid to even speak!
But the earth remembers what the law forgot,
And we are the only ones who can untie the knot!

[Chorus]
It’s an orchestrated divide!
Keep the weary working class looking side to side!
If we never look up, we will never see the crown,
Just another generation, beaten out and broken down.
But we will not stay down.

[Outro]
We will not stay down.
pull_quotes: They built the fences high, but they built the anger higher,
Drowning out the truth with the beating of their drums.

tracks.title: The Common Good
tracks.summary: The contrast between ancient community land rights and modern deprivation.
tracks.narrative_role: The contrast between ancient community land rights and modern deprivation.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The grass was green and the river was free,
A grant to the burgh from the ancient decree.
We walked on the soil that belonged to us all,
Before they built up the iron and the stone wall.
Now the ledger is heavy, the pockets are lined,
Leaving the folk and the working class blind.

[Chorus]
Where is the common good? Where did it go?
Traded away for the corporate show.
They fenced off the heather, they metered the wood,
And sold off the soul of the common good.

[Verse 2]
The aldermen smile and they sign on the line,
Trading our birthright for a private design.
I pluck on these strings and I beat on the skin,
Watching the thieves and the barons roll in.
We’re strangers now on the land of our birth,
Priced right out of the ancient earth.

[Chorus]
Where is the common good? Where did it go?
Traded away for the corporate show.
They fenced off the heather, they metered the wood,
And sold off the soul of the common good.

[Bridge]
They cannot buy the wind! They cannot own the rain!
They cannot wash the blood from the stolen domain!
The earth will remember the sovereign's claim!

[Outro]
The common good. They sold the common good.
pull_quotes: The grass was green and the river was free,
I pluck on these strings and I beat on the skin,

tracks.title: Shadows on Holyrood
tracks.summary: The illusion of domestic political power and devolved parliaments.
tracks.narrative_role: The illusion of domestic political power and devolved parliaments.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I walked to the parliament, shiny and braw,
Looking for men who could stand for the law.
But the suits in the chamber, they argue and preen,
Playing their parts on a power-less screen.
They promise us rain, but they cannot make clouds,
They whisper of freedom to pacify crowds.

[Chorus]
It’s naught but a shadow on Holyrood stone!
A ghost of a sovereign, bound up in a chain!
They hold up the gavel, but they do not hold sway,
While the masters in Westminster dictate the play!
Yes, the masters in Westminster dictate the play.

[Verse 2]
The aldermen bicker over pennies and dust,
While the steel of our industry crumbles to rust.
They sit in their seats, and they rubber-stamp pain,
Content with an umbrella under the rain.
A parliament built with a lock on the door,
To keep out the wind and the cries of the poor.

[Chorus]
It’s naught but a shadow on Holyrood stone!
A ghost of a sovereign, bound up in a chain!
They hold up the gavel, but they do not hold sway,
While the masters in Westminster dictate the play!
Yes, the masters in Westminster dictate the play.

[Bridge]
Electing a shadow will not bring in the sun!
The illusion is fading, the damage is done!
We are asking for bread from a painted-on wall,
Waiting for echoes to answer the call!

[Chorus]
It’s naught but a shadow on Holyrood stone!
A ghost of a sovereign, bound up in a chain!
They hold up the gavel, but they do not hold sway,
While the masters in Westminster dictate the play!
Yes, the masters in Westminster dictate the play.

[Outro]
Look past the shadow. Look past the stone.
pull_quotes: I walked to the parliament, shiny and braw,
To keep out the wind and the cries of the poor.

tracks.title: 1707 (The Annexation)
tracks.act_title: Act II: Descent into the Archives
tracks.summary: The Treaty of Union and the historical betrayal of the nation.
tracks.narrative_role: The Treaty of Union and the historical betrayal of the nation.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The dust is thick on the archive floor,
A hidden lock on a heavy door.
I read the lines they tried to hide,
The ink that swallowed a nation's pride.
They passed the gold to the chosen few,
And sold the land that the people knew.

[Chorus]
Seventeen oh seven, the grand deceit!
An annexation wrapped in a winding sheet!
They dressed it up as a partner's vow,
But the master's hand is heavy now!
Yes, a voluntary lie to bind the free,
To drown the truth in the dark, cold sea!

[Verse 2]
The Claim of Right was pushed aside,
While the traitors cheered and the people cried.
They traded sovereignty for a velvet chair,
And left us gasping for our own air.
A parliament bought with a heavy purse,
Delivering a three-hundred-year-old curse.

[Chorus]
Seventeen oh seven, the grand deceit!
An annexation wrapped in a winding sheet!
They dressed it up as a partner's vow,
But the master's hand is heavy now!
Yes, a voluntary lie to bind the free,
To drown the truth in the dark, cold sea!

[Bridge]
They stitched the flags and they forged the chain!
They took the power but they left the pain!
It was never a union, it was just a cage!
Written in blood on a stolen page!

[Chorus]
Seventeen oh seven, the grand deceit!
An annexation wrapped in a winding sheet!
They dressed it up as a partner's vow,
But the master's hand is heavy now!
Yes, a voluntary lie to bind the free,
To drown the truth in the dark, cold sea!

[Outro]
Just a voluntary lie.
pull_quotes: The dust is thick on the archive floor,
Delivering a three-hundred-year-old curse.

tracks.title: Freeport Lullaby
tracks.act_title: Act II: Descent into the Archives
tracks.summary: Corporate feudalism and the modern theft of territorial sovereignty.
tracks.narrative_role: Corporate feudalism and the modern theft of territorial sovereignty.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
They drew a line around the coast in the dead of the night,
A boundary for the corporate ghost, blocking out the light.
No law of the land down here, no tax to pay,
Just the profit drawn from the marrow of the day.

[Chorus]
Hush now, child, in the Freeport night.
They have traded the dawn for a neon light.
The soil is sold, the gates are locked,
Our sovereignty is just a stock.
A lullaby for a nation chained.

[Verse 2]
Steel fences rise up high where the barley grew,
And the common good is a stolen dream for few.
The workers march real slow to the engine's hum,
Waiting on a train of justice that will never come.

[Chorus]
Hush now, child, in the Freeport night.
They have traded the dawn for a neon light.
The soil is sold, the gates are locked,
Our sovereignty is just a stock.
A lullaby for a nation chained.

[Bridge]
Hush now, child, in the Freeport night!
They have traded the dawn for a neon light!
The soil is sold, the gates are locked,
Our sovereignty is just a stock.
A lullaby for a nation chained.

[Outro]
Where only the corporate hand has reigned.
pull_quotes: They drew a line around the coast in the dead of the night,
Waiting on a train of justice that will never come.

tracks.title: Chimera
tracks.act_title: Act II: Descent into the Archives
tracks.summary: The suppression of the Claim of Right by the domestic legal system.
tracks.narrative_role: The suppression of the Claim of Right by the domestic legal system.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I pulled the parchment from the dust and the stone,
The Claim of Right that said this earth was our own.
It swore the sovereign voice belonged to you and me,
A promise that the folk were unbound, forever free.
But ink on a hidden page is just a withered skin...
When the lords in the high court will not let the justice in.

[Chorus]
It’s a legal chimera!
A phantom walking the hall!
A shadow painted on a bricked-up wall.
They hold the gavel, they rig the heavy game,
Locking away the constitution, leaving us only the name.
Yes, they smile and call us sovereign...
While they wrap us in the chain.

[Verse 2]
I carried the words to the keepers of the gate.
They stared with hollow eyes, sealing the nation's fate.
"Non-justiciable," they whispered, a relic of the past.
Just an illusion, son, it was never meant to last.
A maze of foreign law to keep the people blind.

[Chorus]
It’s a legal chimera!
A phantom walking the hall!
A shadow painted on a bricked-up wall.
They hold the gavel, they rig the heavy game,
Locking away the constitution, leaving us only the name.
Yes, they smile and call us sovereign...
While they wrap us in the chain.

[Bridge]
You cannot seek for justice in the house that stole the deed!
You cannot ask the parasite to cure the host it bleeds!
The system isn't broken... it's working as designed!
To leave the sovereign people forever left behind!

[Chorus]
Just a legal chimera.
A phantom in the hall.
A shadow painted on a bricked-up wall.
They hold the gavel, they rig the heavy game,
Locking away the constitution, leaving us only the name.

[Outro]
Just a chimera in the dark.
pull_quotes: I pulled the parchment from the dust and the stone,
A maze of foreign law to keep the people blind.

tracks.title: The Archivist's Midnight
tracks.act_title: Act II: Descent into the Archives
tracks.summary: The turning point in the archives; the darkest hour before dawn.
tracks.narrative_role: The turning point in the archives; the darkest hour before dawn.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The candle burns low, the shadows stretch tall
Dancing like ghosts on the archive wall.
A mountain of parchment, a river of dust...
Searching for something a man could trust.
I pull at the threads of a broken decree.

[Chorus]
Oh, the archivist's midnight is bitter and cold,
Reading the lies that the centuries told.
They buried the truth beneath a mountain of stone,
Leaving the folk to carry the pain.
Yes, we carry the pain.

[Verse 2]
The words blur together, the ink starts to fade
Trapped in the dark of a deal that was made.
I’m looking for loopholes, a crack in the wall,
Just a whisper of justice to answer the call.
But the ledgers are sealed, the pages are numb.

[Chorus]
Oh, the archivist's midnight is bitter and cold,
Reading the lies that the centuries told.
They buried the truth beneath a mountain of stone,
Leaving the folk to carry the pain.
Yes, we carry the pain.

[Bridge]
There must be a spark in the ashes of old!
A story of freedom that has not been sold!
I will not surrender the ghost to the night,
I'll keep digging deep till I uncover the right!

[Outro]
Keep digging deep.
Till we uncover the right.
pull_quotes: The candle burns low, the shadows stretch tall
Just a whisper of justice to answer the call.

tracks.title: Salvo Jure Cujuslibet
tracks.summary: The emotional turning point. The protagonist translates the ancient Latin principle, discovering the legal defense of the people.
tracks.narrative_role: The emotional turning point. The protagonist translates the ancient Latin principle, discovering the legal defense of the people.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I ran my finger cross the faded ink,
A heavy truth upon the ruin's brink.
A final clause before the session closed,
A shield against the power they imposed.
Salvo jure cujuslibet, the ancient letters read,
A lifeline pulling backward from the dead.

[Pre-Chorus]
It means they cannot steal what isn't theirs to take.
It means the sovereign bond is one they cannot break.

[Chorus]
Saving the right of anyone!
Before the gavel falls and the day is done!
No parliament can wash the sovereign claim away,
The people hold the crown above the law!
Yes, the people hold the crown above the law!

[Verse 2]
For centuries they kept the safety net unseen,
Behind a painted curtain and a velvet screen.
They passed their acts and signed the land away,
But left the rightful owners in the grey.
The act of salvo stands to catch the ones they left behind,
To break the heavy chains that keep us blind.

[Pre-Chorus]
It means they cannot steal what isn't theirs to take.
It means the sovereign bond is one they cannot break.

[Chorus]
Saving the right of anyone!
Before the gavel falls and the day is done!
No parliament can wash the sovereign claim away,
The people hold the crown above the law!
Yes, the people hold the crown above the law!

[Bridge]
[Chorus]
Saving the right of anyone!
Before the gavel falls and the day is done!
No parliament can wash the sovereign claim away,
The people hold the crown above the law!
Yes, the people hold the crown above the law!

[Outro]
Salvo jure cujuslibet.
pull_quotes: I ran my finger cross the faded ink,
But left the rightful owners in the grey.

tracks.title: Healing the Divide
tracks.summary: Overcoming orchestrated division to unite under a common cause.
tracks.narrative_role: Overcoming orchestrated division to unite under a common cause.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I walked back out into the clearing light,
Leaving the dust and the ghosts of the night.
I looked at the faces, worn down by the grind,
Fighting each other, intentionally blind.
They taught us to bicker over scraps on the floor,
While they stole the whole house and padlocked the door.

[Pre-Chorus]
But the parchment is clear and the ancient law stands!
The power was never removed from our hands!

[Chorus]
So let go of the anger that keeps us apart!
We share the same struggle, we beat the same heart!
If we stand all together, the shadows will break,
For the sake of the sovereign, it's time to awake!
Yes, it's time to awake!

[Verse 2]
The left and the right, it's a fabricated game,
A trick of the crown to keep everything the same.
While we argue the borders they drew in the sand,
They strip-mine the spirit and sell off the land.
But the truth is a weapon they cannot withstand,
When it's held by a unified, sovereign band.

[Pre-Chorus]
But the parchment is clear and the ancient law stands!
The power was never removed from our hands!

[Chorus]
So let go of the anger that keeps us apart!
We share the same struggle, we beat the same heart!
If we stand all together, the shadows will break,
For the sake of the sovereign, it's time to awake!
Yes, it's time to awake!

[Bridge]
[Chorus]
So let go of the anger that keeps us apart!
We share the same struggle, we beat the same heart!
If we stand all together, the shadows will break,
For the sake of the sovereign, it's time to awake!
Yes, it's time to awake!

[Outro]
Time to awake.
pull_quotes: I walked back out into the clearing light,
They strip-mine the spirit and sell off the land.

tracks.title: The Stirling Directive
tracks.summary: Unstoppable democratic momentum. The people are no longer asking; they are instructing their parliament.
tracks.narrative_role: Unstoppable democratic momentum. The people are no longer asking; they are instructing their parliament.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
We did not come to beg outside the heavy gate,
We came to take the ledger and rewrite the fate.
The time for asking questions in the dark is done,
We are standing all together in the rising sun.
You thought the sovereign spirit was a broken thing,
But listen to the chorus that the people sing!

[Pre-Chorus]
The Claim of Right is breathing in the modern air!
We are ending the illusion, and we are stripping it bare!

[Chorus]
Deliver the directive! Lay the parchment down!
We are taking back the power from the foreign crown!
The parliament is serving at the people's will,
We are echoing the thunder on the Stirling hill!
Yes, the sovereignty is ours, and we hold it still!

[Verse 2]
Send word into the chambers where the shadows play,
Tell Westminster their edicts hold no heavy sway.
The union was an annexation, bought and sold,
But we refuse to suffer in the bitter cold.
We are breaking up the system that was built to bind,
Leaving the division and the fear behind.

[Pre-Chorus]
The Claim of Right is breathing in the modern air!
We are ending the illusion, and we are stripping it bare!

[Chorus]
Deliver the directive! Lay the parchment down!
We are taking back the power from the foreign crown!
The parliament is serving at the people's will,
We are echoing the thunder on the Stirling hill!
Yes, the sovereignty is ours, and we hold it still!

[Bridge]
[Chorus]
Deliver the directive! Lay the parchment down!
We are taking back the power from the foreign crown!
The parliament is serving at the people's will,
We are echoing the thunder on the Stirling hill!
Yes, the sovereignty is ours, and we hold it still!

[Outro]
We hold it still.
pull_quotes: We did not come to beg outside the heavy gate,
But we refuse to suffer in the bitter cold.

tracks.title: Echoes of Arbroath
tracks.summary: The unbroken chain of sovereignty throughout history.
tracks.narrative_role: The unbroken chain of sovereignty throughout history.
tracks.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Seven hundred years have scattered on the breeze,
Since the abbots and the barons made their pleas.
In the quiet halls of Arbroath, they set the parchment down,
To swear the sovereign people are themselves the rightful crown.
A king is but an equal, who serves the people's cry,
And the spirit of that letter will never truly die.

[Chorus]
As long as but a hundred of us remain alive,
The ancient flame of liberty will manage to survive.
We will never bow the knee to any foreign hand,
For the unbroken chain of sovereignty is rooted in the land.
Yes, the unbroken chain is rooted in the land.

[Verse 2]
They try to tell us now that history is a ghost,
A forgotten little shadow on a subjugated coast.
But the earth remembers thirteen twenty in the marrow of the stone,
The declaration echoes that we stand and fall alone.
When monarchs break the sacred oath, they're stripped of all their pride,
For the soul of independence has never really died.

[Chorus]
As long as but a hundred of us remain alive,
The ancient flame of liberty will manage to survive.
We will never bow the knee to any foreign hand,
For the unbroken chain of sovereignty is rooted in the land.
Yes, the unbroken chain is rooted in the land.

[Bridge]
The kings have turned to ashes, the empires fall to rust,
But the will of everyday folk is a sacred, heavy trust.
Through the highland rain and the howling winter wind,
We carry forth the fire that our ancestors pinned.

[Chorus]
As long as but a hundred of us remain alive,
The ancient flame of liberty will manage to survive.
We will never bow the knee to any foreign hand,
For the unbroken chain of sovereignty is rooted in the land.
Yes, the unbroken chain is rooted in the land.

[Outro]
Rooted in the land.
pull_quotes: Seven hundred years have scattered on the breeze,
For the soul of independence has never really died.

The fire has settled, the embers are bright,
